What I help with

Dyslexia, dyspraxia & learning difficulties

Reading, writing, handwriting or coordination.

What it is

Some children find reading, writing, handwriting or coordination much harder than their classmates, even when they are trying their very best.

Learning difficulties have nothing to do with intelligence. Many children with dyslexia or dyspraxia are bright and creative, but need a different way in.

Common signs

  • Difficulty with reading or spelling
  • Slow or untidy handwriting
  • Clumsiness or coordination difficulties
  • Falling behind at school
  • Low confidence about learning
When to get help: If your child is falling behind despite their effort, or losing confidence about school, an assessment can explain why and what helps.

How I can help

Assessment and a written report, practical strategies (including "Handwriting: cracking the code and mastering the skills") and support with confidence.

Things you can try today

Read together for short, regular periods
Use multi-sensory learning: seeing, hearing and doing
Focus on strengths as well as difficulties
Talk to your child’s teacher early

What happens next

  1. Get in touchCall or message me on WhatsApp or Viber, in Bulgarian or English.
  2. A first conversationWe talk about what’s going on and what you’d like to change.
  3. A plan that fits youWe agree goals together, online or in person.
  4. Regular reviewsWe check progress along the way and adjust as needed.

Questions

What happens in an assessment?

We meet, I use structured tasks suited to your child’s age, and you receive a written report with clear recommendations.

Can the report be shared with school?

Yes. Reports are written so that parents and teachers can use them.
